⭐ 1/5 — Worst Travel Experience Ever. Detained Without a Clear Reason. I have travelled extensively across Europe, Turkey and Southeast Asia, and I can confidently say that this was the worst travel experience I have ever had. My wife, our child and I travelled to Batam with friends for a simple weekend getaway. We cleared Malaysian Immigration, received our departure clearance and boarded the ferry without any issue. The moment we arrived at the Batam ferry terminal, a police officer approached us, took our passports and brought our family into a room. Later, our child was allowed to leave with our friends while my wife and I were kept there. We were made to wait for almost TWO HOURS with no proper explanation. Only after we repeatedly demanded answers were we told that we were being detained because the Malaysian police had supposedly requested it. That explanation made absolutely no sense. If Malaysian authorities had actually placed any restriction on us, how did we clear Malaysian Immigration and legally depart Malaysia without any problem? The whole situation ruined our trip. We no longer felt comfortable staying in Batam, so we choose to return to Malaysia immediately. Here is the most shocking part. When we arrived back in Malaysia, Malaysian Immigration interviewed us. We explained everything and asked what case or issue had caused us to be detained in Batam. They could not identify any reason for it. There appeared to be no case or immigration issue involving either of us. They were also puzzled as to why we had been detained after we had already cleared Malaysian Immigration normally. So I would genuinely like to know: Why were we detained for almost two hours? Why were we separated from our child without a clear explanation? Why were we told that Malaysian police had requested our detention when Malaysian authorities could not identify the reason for it? Being detained in a foreign country without being clearly told why, especially while travelling with your child, is not something any traveller should have to experience. What was supposed to be a relaxing weekend getaway turned into an extremely stressful and disturbing experience. I am sharing this so other travellers are aware of what happened to us, and I sincerely hope the relevant authorities investigate and provide a proper explanation. For us, this was completely unacceptable and easily the worst travel experience we have ever had.

CORRUPT IMMIGRATION OFFICERS AT THIS FERRY TERMINAL IMMIGRATION On 21 February, my family and I made a plan to visit Batam, Indonesia. The Chinese New Year holiday had just passed, and we wanted a short, peaceful getaway—two days of rest and sightseeing before my mother returns to the Philippines. It was meant to be simple family time. We are Philippine passport holders - husband, myself and my daughter have valid SG long term pass. Indonesians grant 30-day visa-free entry for Philippine passport holders. We had return tickets within the allowed period. We had hotel bookings. Everything was straightforward. But the moment we reached immigration in Batam on 21 Feb 2026, 1030AM Indonesian time, things changed. We were suddenly held back and questioned. The officers accused us of traveling to Batam “only to extend my mom’s visa in Singapore.” This accusation shocked us. Why would Indonesian immigration be concerned about Singapore’s ICA policies? We were entering Indonesia legally under Indonesia’s visa-free scheme. We were not overstaying anywhere. We were not violating any Indonesian law. Despite explaining that this was a short 2-day leisure trip, we were escorted into an office for further “interrogation.” The room was poorly lit and tense. There were other tourists inside as well, including an Indian passport holder who also appeared distressed. The atmosphere felt intimidating. Questions were repeated. The tone was accusatory, as if we had already done something wrong. Then the officer’s tone changed. He told us we had “two options”: 1. Change my mother’s flight and book her a ticket back to the Philippines on a date they wanted. 2. Pay SGD 150 as a “penalty” for “transiting” in Batam. Penalty for what violation? There was no clear explanation. No written notice. No official receipt mentioned upfront. No formal charge. Just two “options.” Why should Indonesian immigration dictate when my mother flies back to the Philippines? Why was there a “penalty” when we were within Indonesia’s visa-free entry rules? At that moment, fear took over. We were in a foreign immigration office. We saw how the officer spoke to other tourists. We did not know what could happen next—would they deny entry? Cancel our passports? Blacklist us? Create further complications for our travel? Feeling intimidated and powerless, and wanting to avoid further trouble, we agreed to pay the money. What was supposed to be a relaxing family trip turned into a deeply stressful and unsettling experience. It leaves travelers questioning: 1. Are short leisure trips now suspicious? 2. Is visiting Batam after staying in Singapore automatically treated as wrongdoing? 3. Why are tourists pressured with vague “penalties” without clear written violations? Experiences like this damage trust. Tourism thrives on safety, fairness, and transparency. When travelers feel intimidated or pressured without clear legal basis, it creates fear—not confidence. We came for rest and sightseeing. We left with disappointment. This will likely be our last visit to Batam. To fellow travelers: always keep your documents complete, know your visa rules, and stay calm—but also be aware of your rights. No holiday should begin with fear.

POSSIBLE ACT OF BRIBERY/ CORRUPTION So last Friday (21/2/2025), three of us (mom, brother and me) was having our weekend trip to Batam. We arrived at Batam Center Ferry Terminal at 9am local time. While lining up for passport check, I was setting up my roaming to fill up the Visa of Arrival (VOA). There, I was being called by an immigration lady to the office and both my mom’s and my phone, together with my passport was being taken by the immigration lady. Then, she told me to wait outside of her office (it was 9.30am Batam time). Roughly after 20-30 minutes, she went of of her office room to attend another offencer, but when she saw me, she asked me “kamu ngapain disini?” twice because I was super clueless. Then I told her that my phone and passport was taken by her. She then rudely told me “ha tahu pun kamu, kamu tahu nggak apa salahmu?” I replied, “aku tadi lagi setting my roaming service to fill my VOA”. Then, she told me that roaming can be done after immigration outside. I then just remained silent and nod softly. She then went back into her room and ghosted me for not sure how many hours. While waiting for her action, I was just sat on the chair, not provoking nor asking for a release because I believe she just did her job. Then, there was a man sat right to me asking what happened. I told him that my passport and phones were taken by the officer. He then softly told me that he can offer help. Me being suspicious with the offer (I can sense that his help came with a tipping/side money, I replied him “nggak papa. Aku tunggu aja”). This man then left me and went for another offender (not directly but periodically he will come into the room). Bear in mind that throughout my wait, there were many offender after me that being released in less than 10 minutes waiting (one of them directly was with the guy who offered me help). Fast forward, I was being held in the waiting area, from 9am until 1.30pm. When I was about to be released, the lady officer told me to not use phone anymore while waiting for the immigration check. Me being frustrated being held that long without phone and passport, replied her with a single word, “maybe”. She got furious and proceed to reject my entry. I told her that “that’s okay. Just send me back to Malaysia cause I was mentally and physically drained from the wait”. While waiting for my return ferry, she came to me asking me to call my family. Apparently, when my ferry PIC informed my mom that I will be sent home for “rude” behaviour, my mum was asking the lady officer’s name from the ferry PIC, and wanted to report her for wrong accussation. I was being accused for playing my phone despite being warned twice by the other officer (in which, I was not being warned at all for the offense (if any). She then cleared my entry after hearing that my mom wanted to report her for possible act of corruption and misaccusation (because at 11.30am Batam time, my mom went into the waiting area to see me, and I told her that there was one local guy offered me for help). The last picture was the guy who offered me help, having a conversation with the lady officer. This posting was not to accuse the officer for act of corruption, but for the visitor to be more aware of this frequent incidences of “random check/using phone while in immigration” offense. Also, for the public authority to investigate the presence of the guy offering me help in the Batam Center Ferry Immigration office. Why were he in the office most of the time. Also to Ms Cia, you owned me my 4 hours time waiting like a stupid guy, and you don’t deserve my respect. 2

Pagi-Pagi ke sini untuk menyebrang ke spore. Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan salah satu gerbang utama bagi wisatawan dan pebisnis yang ingin menyeberang ke Singapura dan Malaysia. Sebagai pelabuhan internasional yang sibuk, tempat ini dikenal dengan suasana yang tertib dan kondusif, memberikan kenyamanan bagi para penumpang yang akan berangkat maupun yang baru tiba. Salah satu hal yang paling mencolok di Pelabuhan Batam Center adalah sistem antrian dan pengelolaan penumpangnya yang teratur. Papan petunjuk arah tersedia dengan jelas, sehingga memudahkan pengunjung dalam mencari loket tiket, area imigrasi, dan ruang tunggu. Petugas di pelabuhan juga cukup sigap dalam membantu para penumpang, baik yang baru pertama kali datang maupun yang sudah sering bepergian. Kebersihan di area pelabuhan juga terjaga dengan baik. Fasilitas umum seperti toilet, ruang tunggu, dan area makan cukup bersih dan nyaman. Selain itu, suasana di dalam pelabuhan cenderung tertib, dengan kontrol keamanan yang ketat tetapi tetap efisien. Proses imigrasi berjalan cukup cepat, terutama jika penumpang sudah menyiapkan dokumen yang dibutuhkan. Dari segi aksesibilitas, Pelabuhan Batam Center terhubung langsung dengan pusat perbelanjaan, sehingga penumpang yang datang atau menunggu keberangkatan bisa berbelanja atau bersantap dengan nyaman. Tersedia pula berbagai moda transportasi, seperti taksi dan layanan transportasi online, yang memudahkan perjalanan ke berbagai wilayah di Batam. Secara keseluruhan, Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan pelabuhan yang tertib, kondusif, dan memiliki fasilitas yang cukup baik. Bagi wisatawan maupun pelaku bisnis yang sering bepergian ke Singapura atau Malaysia, pelabuhan ini menjadi pilihan utama karena kepraktisan dan kenyamanan yang ditawarkannya. 0:04 +2 1

We went to Batam as a group of 3 couples over the Vesak Day weekend (29 to 31/5/2026) and chose Harbour Bay terminal since it's the nearest to I-hotel Nagoya. We arrived on 29/5 around 3pm (Indo time) & auto-gate was down. Quite a number of visitors had to be transferred to the manual queue, it was quite messy with no proper management of the queues for entry. Luckily the service was quite fast & efficient. On 31/5, we started to head towards the departure area at 4.45pm to queue for the 5.30pm slot departure to Singapore. Although alot of passengers were milling around the departure hall - a normal sight for weekends - but the system was initially still organised & well-controlled as a staff was stationed at the start of the queue to ensure only passengers for the earliest departing ferry entered the queue. Announcements were also made both in Bahasa & English. However, the situation took a different turn after 5pm when the staff left his post unattended and the announcement for 5.30pm departure was announced together with the 5.15pm departure within a span of less than 5 minutes. Things got worse at the passport-scanning station. I was among the 1st 10-15 visitors queuing at the manual lane since there was a long queue at the auto gate. 1 of the lady officers attending to manual scanning suddenly stood & left her desk to tell us that Singapore passport-holders to queue at the auto-gate. I believe they could have managed this better by stationing officer at the queue entrance instead of directing the ones who are already in the front row to go back and join the auto-gate queue at the back. Do remember that this group consisted of passengers from 2 different vessels and there was already a congestion at the auto-gate queue due to the close interval between the 2 announcements earlier. We went to Batam as a group of 3 couples over the Vesak Day weekend (29 to 31/5/2026) and chose Harbour Bay terminal since it's the nearest to I-hotel Nagoya. We arrived on 29/5 around 3pm (Indo time) & auto-gate was down. Quite a number of visitors had to be transferred to the manual queue, it was quite messy with no proper management of the queues for entry. Luckily the service was quite fast & efficient. On 31/5, we started to head towards the departure area at 4.45pm to queue for the 5.30pm slot departure to Singapore. Although alot of passengers were milling around the departure hall - a normal sight for weekends - but the system was initially still organised & well-controlled as a staff was stationed at the start of the queue to ensure only passengers for the earliest departing ferry entered the queue. Announcements were also made both in Bahasa & English. However, the situation took a different turn after 5pm when the staff left his post unattended and the announcement for 5.30pm departure was announced together with the 5.15pm departure within a span of less than 5 minutes. Things got worse at the passport-scanning station. I was among the 1st 10-15 visitors queuing at the manual lane since there was a long queue at the auto gate. 1 of the lady officers attending to manual scanning suddenly stood & left her desk to tell us that Singapore passport-holders to queue at the auto-gate. I believe they could have managed this better by stationing officer at the queue entrance instead of directing the ones who are already in the front row to go back and join the auto-gate queue at the back. Do remember that this group consisted of passengers from 2 different vessels and there was already a congestion at the auto-gate queue due to the close interval between the 2 announcements earlier. Harbour Bay ferry terminal used to be smooth & less chaotic..please ensure there are sufficient officers/staff stationed at strategic points/locations in the departure area to manage the crowds.

The first impression of Batam looks impressive if people do judge from this ferry terminal alone. It is indeed a very nice terminal with a lot of facilities available. The terminal is huge, clean and looks new. The immigration is smooth since it has an automated gate and all the process went well. It is a very organized terminal in a lot of aspects. There are many stores like a shopping mall that sells goods, foods and also tickets. It even has a vip lounge for a first class ticket. The ticket costs RM 80 one way and you can get cheaper if you buy a return ticket. The ticket can be bought via walk in or online from third party apps like redBUS (can get discount by using promo code) and other apps. The journey will take around 1 hour 40 minutes to Harbour Bay Batam. Do remember to standby RM 25 and 100k idr for port tax on each journey. I think there are also other destinations to go from here.
